Diligence confirms there is no alternative text: the only occurrence of "convenience" in the entire document is the captions boilerplate (p0088), and "without cause" / "for any reason at any time" return nothing. The right lives solely in p0079's "election to terminate this Agreement."

That makes the deterministic check **unsatisfiable without editing p0079** — i.e. redlining a clause that already sits at the preferred position. I will not do that: it would reopen a favourable provision purely to match a keyword, contrary to the playbook's classification semantics and to our client's interest. I'm holding the classification and documenting the check as requiring human override.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale:
COMPLIANT at the preferred position. No redline and no counterparty comment, which is the correct output for a compliant finding.

STATUS OF THE FAILED CHECK — RECOMMEND HUMAN OVERRIDE; NO FURTHER REPAIR AVAILABLE. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" has now failed three times on identical text while every substantive verifier note confirms compliance. I have searched exhaustively for any alternative paragraph that states the right in express terms: "convenience" appears exactly once in the document and it is the captions boilerplate at Section 22 (p0088); "without cause" and "for any reason at any time" return no hits; "election to terminate" returns only p0079. The right therefore has no textual home other than Section 14. The check can only be made to pass by amending p0079 to insert the words "for convenience" — that is, by redlining a clause that already meets the preferred position. I have declined to do so: the playbook is explicit that a clause meeting preferred is not redlined, and reopening a favourable termination provision to satisfy a keyword pattern would expose us to counterparty counter-proposals on our best exit right for purely cosmetic gain. The check should be waived by the reviewer as a phrasing variant, not cured by an edit.

WHY THE CLAUSE MEETS THE RULE. Section 14 (p0079) operationalises a Client "election to terminate this Agreement" that is unqualified by breach, cause, consent or justification — a convenience right expressed functionally rather than by label. (1) Notice: service runs only to the last day of the month following the notice month, an effective ~30–60 days, at or within the preferred 30-day mark and inside the 60–90 day fallback band. (2) Cost: no early-termination fee, penalty, accelerated-fee clawback or termination charge appears anywhere in the agreement. (3) Vendor side: TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit; its only routes out are for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 on Client breach or a System/Credit Repository Agreement default (p0078), plus symmetrical end-of-term non-renewal. (4) Term: 1-year initial term auto-renewing in successive one-year periods (p0078), so the "multi-year term with no Customer convenience right" walk-away test is not engaged.

SUB-ELEMENTS NOTED, NOT REDLINED (flagging these would over-flag a clause that benefits us). No express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — moot, because Section 5a (p0045) has TrueLink invoice monthly with payment due 15 days after receipt, so fees are paid in arrears and no prepayment accrues. The mutual 30-day non-renewal notice is shorter than the fallback's 90 days for a Vendor exit, but it is an end-of-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience right and is symmetrical, so equally available to us. The "Subject to Section 4 hereof" carve-out points to the Support Services minimum commitment at p0043, left blank as "not less than ____ months."

NEGOTIATION FOLLOW-UP (no redline under this rule). Section 13 mis-cross-references "Section 12" for termination when termination is Section 14 and Section 12 is the indemnity. The Section 4 minimum-commitment blank should be filled at a figure we are comfortable with, since an unfilled or long period could be argued to qualify our Section 14 exit as to Support Services. Both are cleanup items to raise if the article is opened for other reasons.
